Read, add, update and delete records

Source: R/records.R
grist_records.Rd

grist_records() reads records from a table into a data frame. The other functions write data frames back to Grist. Large writes are split into several requests (see grist_write_options()).

Usage

grist_records(
  doc,
  table,
  filter = NULL,
  sort = NULL,
  limit = NULL,
  convert = c("auto", "basic", "raw"),
  options = NULL
)

grist_records_add(
  doc,
  table,
  data,
  convert = c("auto", "basic", "raw"),
  options = NULL
)

grist_records_update(
  doc,
  table,
  data,
  convert = c("auto", "basic", "raw"),
  options = NULL
)

grist_records_upsert(
  doc,
  table,
  data,
  by,
  mode = c("upsert", "update", "insert"),
  onmany = c("first", "all", "none"),
  convert = c("auto", "basic", "raw"),
  options = NULL
)

grist_records_delete(doc, table, ids, options = NULL)

Arguments

doc

A grist_doc object, document ID or document URL. See grist_doc().

table

Table ID, as listed by grist_tables().

filter

A named list mapping column IDs to allowed values, e.g. list(status = c("open", "new")). Rows must match every column.

sort

Character vector of column IDs to sort by. Prefix a column with - for descending order, e.g. c("status", "-priority"). Use "manualSort" for the order set in the Grist interface.

limit

Maximum number of rows to return. NULL returns all rows.

convert

How to convert cell values: "auto", "basic" or "raw". See the section "Type conversion".

options

A grist_read_options() object (or grist_write_options() for the writing functions). If NULL, the default set with options(gristmillr.read_options = ) or options(gristmillr.write_options = ) is used.

data

A data frame of records. For grist_records_add(), each column must be a column of the Grist table. For grist_records_update(), data must also have an integer id column.

by

Character vector of columns that identify a record, such as "email". Each row of data is matched against the table on these columns. data must contain them, with no missing values and no duplicated combinations.

mode

What to do with each row of data: "upsert" updates the record with matching by values and adds a record if there is none. "update" only updates matching records and skips rows that match nothing. "insert" only adds records and skips rows that already match. Grist does not report which rows were skipped.

onmany

What to do when several records in the table match one row of data: update the "first" one, update "all" of them, or update "none" of them.

ids

Row IDs to delete, either an integer vector or a data frame with an id column (such as the result of grist_records()).

Value

grist_records() returns a data frame whose first column id is the row ID. grist_records_add() returns the new row IDs. grist_records_update(), grist_records_upsert() and grist_records_delete() return doc. All but grist_records() return invisibly.

Type conversion

The convert argument controls how cell values are translated between Grist and R:

  • "auto" (the default) fetches the table's column types with grist_columns() and converts every column: Int to integer, Numeric to double, Bool to logical, Date to Date, DateTime to POSIXct, Text and Choice to character, Ref to integer row IDs, and ChoiceList, RefList and Attachments to list-columns of vectors. Columns whose cells don't match their declared type are returned unconverted with a warning.

  • "basic" does not fetch column types. Scalar values are simplified and ["L", ...] lists become list-columns, but dates stay numeric (seconds since the epoch) and references stay integer IDs. When writing, R dates, date-times and factors are still converted.

  • "raw" returns or sends cell values exactly as the API does, as list-columns.

Empty values

Grist stores an empty Bool cell as FALSE, so an NA written to a Bool column is read back as FALSE. Empty Int, Numeric, Date and DateTime cells are read back as NA.

See also

Other records: grist_resolve_refs(), grist_sql()

Examples

if (FALSE) {
doc <- grist_doc("am2iHJ9Amvo7Ve3EE5emtu")

grist_records(doc, "Pets")
grist_records(doc, "Pets", filter = list(pet = "cat"), sort = "-popularity")

new <- data.frame(pet = c("cat", "dog"), popularity = c(67L, 95L))
ids <- grist_records_add(doc, "Pets", new)

grist_records_update(doc, "Pets", data.frame(id = ids, popularity = 1L))

# Match on a column instead of the row ID: update cats, add rabbits
pets <- data.frame(pet = c("cat", "rabbit"), popularity = c(70L, 40L))
grist_records_upsert(doc, "Pets", pets, by = "pet")
grist_records_delete(doc, "Pets", ids)
}
